question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Location and geography of the Battle of Colachel, 1741]
options: Colachel — Coastal town in present-day Tamil Nadu (Kanyakumari district)
Travancore — Kingdom that defeated the Dutch at Colachel under Marthanda Varma
Cape Comorin (Kanyakumari) — Southernmost tip of India, near the battle site
Cochin — Location where the Battle of Colachel was primarily fought
wrong_fact: The Battle of Colachel was fought at Colachel, a port town on the southwestern tip of the Indian peninsula in present-day Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu — NOT at Cochin (Kerala). Cochin was a separate Dutch trading post that was lost later.
explanation: Colachel is a small coastal town near Cape Comorin (Kanyakumari) in Tamil Nadu. The battle in 1741 was between the Kingdom of Travancore under Marthanda Varma and the Dutch East India Company (VOC). Cochin (Kochi) is a different port city in Kerala and was the site of a separate Dutch settlement, not where the battle occurred.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Aftermath and Treaty of Mavelikkara following the Battle of Colachel]
options: Treaty of Mavelikkara (1753) — Signed between Travancore and the Dutch, ending hostilities
Mavelikkara — Town in present-day Alappuzha district of Kerala where the treaty was signed
Dutch prisoners — Some Dutch soldiers including Eustachius De Lannoy served Travancore after capture
Pondicherry — Ceded to Travancore by the Dutch as part of the Treaty of Mavelikkara
wrong_fact: Pondicherry was never ceded to Travancore; it was a French territory (French India). The Treaty of Mavelikkara required the Dutch to give up all claims to Travancore, release prisoners, and cease interfering in Kerala affairs. Pondicherry remained French until 1954.
explanation: The Treaty of Mavelikkara (1753) was signed at Mavelikkara in present-day Kerala between Travancore and the Dutch. Dutch POWs, including naval officer Eustachius De Lannoy, were absorbed into the Travancore navy. The Dutch did NOT cede Pondicherry — that was a separate French settlement that had nothing to do with the Dutch-Travancore conflict.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch naval strategy and positions in South India around the time of the Battle of Colachel, 1741]
options: Colachel harbour — Dutch attempted to blockade Travancore's southwestern coast
Quilon (Kollam) — Dutch had a factory here on the Malabar Coast before Colachel
Calicut (Kozhikode) — Dutch established a significant factory here as their main South Indian base
Cochin — Dutch stronghold inherited from the Portuguese, a key base in Kerala
wrong_fact: Calicut (Kozhikode) was NOT the Dutch main base in South India; it was historically associated with the Zamorin and was primarily a Portuguese and later British contact point. The Dutch main base in South India was Cochin (seized from Portugal in 1663), and they had factories at Quilon and other Malabar ports.
explanation: Dutch operations in South India were centred on Cochin (captured from the Portuguese in 1663), with subsidiary factories at Quilon, Cannanore, and Cranganore. Colachel was the point of their naval assault on Travancore. Calicut was important historically but was not established as the Dutch main base — Cochin was the primary Dutch administrative centre on the Malabar Coast.
